liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Terrapin Station (First One!)** (3 reviews): Phil's bass lines stand out in Terrapin Station, which is a first performance, as is Estimated Prophet; Garcia explores more in the first solo and in the jam linking Lady With a Fan to Terrapin [16][18][21]
- **Help On The Way** (2 reviews): Hot Help on the Way > Slipknot, and Estimated Prophet is the first of its kind; Help > Slipknot > Franklin's Tower is the reviewer's favorite part of the show [14][17]
- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): Keith plays a beautiful solo in They Love Each Other [15]
- **Deal** (1 review): Jerry takes a great solo in Deal, and Phil's bass is also strong there [16]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): Rare Playin' > Wheel > Playin' sequence closes set one, with jamming the reviewer calls incredible [14]
- **Sampson And Delilah** (1 review): Sampson and Delilah is singled out as a highlight [16]
- **Slipknot!** (1 review): Help/Slipknot is energetic and powerful, climbing steadily [19]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Franklin's Tower has delightful China Cat teases that ease the tension left by Slipknot [19]

## Setlist highlights

- **Technical Difficulties + Tune Up**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]

## The recordings

- **gd77-02-26.sbd.owen.23808.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 195 min; rated 4.95/5 by 40 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer prefers this to the other circulating soundboard, finding it sounds much better; After hearing both soundboards, reviewer finds this one sounds much better [20][22]
- **gd1977-02-26.sbd.wizard.32009.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 195 min; rated 4.2/5 by 5 [3]. Said about its sound: Uploader calls this the older of two soundboards, finding it has better dynamics than the highly compressed newer one [3]
- **gd1977-02-26.sbd.steve.253.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 170 min; rated 4/5 by 12 [6]. Said about its sound: Uploader says it sounds incredible but has a few dropouts and reel changes; Dropouts are noted in Samson and Delilah at 1:54 and Music Never Stopped at 2:04 [6]
- **gd77-02-26.sbd.alphadog.9752.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 161 min; rated 4.72/5 by 176 [11]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds it less smooth than later versions, with edgier guitars [18]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says liquid bottles first appeared at this show [23]
- Rick Griffin's huge mural of a bony claw holding a scroll was hoisted behind the stage [23]
- Griffin, Jose Kent and Richard Lippincott hung the mural without the band knowing; it vanished after the show [23]
- Tuning and stage chatter have been preserved in this transfer [4]
- Reviewer ranks it among their five favorite 1977 shows, as the year's opening show [14]
- Called one of 1977's best shows, and the first show of that year [15]
- Reviewer says this show can make you forget the over-rated month of May 1977 [17]
- Garcia seems to be trying ideas before settling on the standard riffs of the May 1977 versions [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd77-02-26.sbd.owen.23808.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Audience patches come from a Sony ECM-280 and TC-153SD chain; tuning patches come from a separate soundboard CD source [1]
- **gd1977-02-26.sbd.wizard.32009.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Owen Brothers; source: SBD>MR>DAT>CD [3]. Also: Most tunings were cut; they were restored from another soundboard source, with audience tape supplying other patches; Audience tape restored the cut start of Estimated and patched glitches in Sugaree and Sampson [3]
- **gd1977-02-26.sbd.steve.253.shnf**: Described as a Betty Board source [6]
- **gd77-02-26.sbd.alphadog.9752.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by AlphaDog; source: Soundboard [11]

## Art and photos

- Poster by SONGLYRICS.com: [Grateful Dead – 1977‐02‐26: Swing Auditorium, San Bernardino, CA, USA](https://www.songlyrics.com/grateful-dead/19770226-swing-auditorium-san-bernardino-ca-usa/) [25]
- Fan art by The Music Never Stopped: [Grateful Dead Live at Swing Auditorium on 02/26/1977](https://dayofthedeadshow.home.blog/2019/02/26/grateful-dead-live-at-swing-auditorium-on-02-26-1977/) [26]
- Fan art by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - Dave's Picks Vol 29: 1977-02-26 Swing Auditorium, San Bernardino, CA](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2019/02/grateful-dead-daves-picks-vol-29-1977.html) [27]
- Poster by Amy Harris: [Bob Weir dies at 78; Grateful Dead played San Bernardino twice](https://www.sbsun.com/2026/01/13/bob-weir-dies-at-78-grateful-dead-played-san-bernardino-twice/) [28]
- Poster by Jerrybase: [Grateful Dead – 1977-02-26](https://jerrybase.com/events/19770226-01) [29]

Reviewer says this show can make you forget the over-rated month of May 1977
Garcia explores more in the first solo and in the jam linking Lady With a Fan to Terrapin
Garcia seems to be trying ideas before settling on the standard riffs of the May 1977 versions
Reviewer finds it less smooth than later versions, with edgier guitars
Help/Slipknot is energetic and powerful, climbing steadily
Franklin's Tower has delightful China Cat teases that ease the tension left by Slipknot
Reviewer prefers this to the other circulating soundboard, finding it sounds much better
Opening Terrapin is treated as the song's first live performance, with a Garcia vocal line quoted
After hearing both soundboards, reviewer finds this one sounds much better
Reviewer says liquid bottles first appeared at this show
Rick Griffin's huge mural of a bony claw holding a scroll was hoisted behind the stage
Griffin, Jose Kent and Richard Lippincott hung the mural without the band knowing; it vanished after the show
Audience patches come from a Sony ECM-280 and TC-153SD chain; tuning patches come from a separate soundboard CD source
Uploader calls this the older of two soundboards, finding it has better dynamics than the highly compressed newer one
Most tunings were cut; they were restored from another soundboard source, with audience tape supplying other patches
Audience tape restored the cut start of Estimated and patched glitches in Sugaree and Sampson
Tuning and stage chatter have been preserved in this transfer
Described as a Betty Board source
Uploader says it sounds incredible but has a few dropouts and reel changes
Dropouts are noted in Samson and Delilah at 1:54 and Music Never Stopped at 2:04
